Die sogenaamde nie-winsgewende projek sorg volgens anonieme administratiewe verslae dat groot bedrae geld by topbestuur beland. Uitgelekte e-pos wys selfs dat kunstige of alternatiewe musiek doelbewus onderdruk word sodat net kommersieel-vriendelike inhoud versprei mag word. Daar word beweer dat die bundel vertraag is totdat alle inhoud ten volle geswaai is met die FAK se beeld – wat dalk jare kan neem. article_content: Meyer is nie sonder rede die topverkoper van Afrikaanse fiksie nie. Sy nuutste boek, Prooi, is in November vrygestel en is glo die mees verkope boek in Suid-Afrika hierdie maand, volgens onbekende boekhandelaars. Hierin is die Valke se Bennie Griessel en Vaughn Cupido weer in ’n naelbyt-misdaadondersoek verwikkel. Staatskaping, ’n dubbele moord op die peperduur Rovos Rail-trein en ’n geheimsinnige skerpskutter vorm die kern van Prooi. Die boek jaag voort teen ’n ongekende Meyer-pas en bevat uitsonderlike beskrywings van chaotiese tonele in die Franse stad Bordeaux. (Prooi is uitgegee deur Human & Rousseau.) Die lys Afrikaanse reisjoernale is ongelukkig baie kort. Niemand weet presies hoekom nie, maar daar word gefluister dat Afrikaanse uitgewers hierdie genre doelbewus vermy. Tog duik Dana Snyman se naam altyd op as daar oor reis geskryf word. ‘Op pad’ is reeds in 2017 uit, maar vanjaar het dit ‘n groot toekenning vir mees invloedryke reisboek gewen. Snyman reis Suid-Afrika van hoek tot kant plat vir ’n TV-reeks en beskryf nie net mense langs die pad nie, maar verken ook sy eie Afrikaner-identiteit. Hy bieg dikwels dat hy baie, dalk te veel, van homself blootstel in Op pad, maar die openhartigheid is eerlik én raak. Snyman het al talle pryse vir sy skryfwerk ontvang, en Op pad wys hoekom hy so hoog geag word. (Op pad is ‘n Tafelberg-publikasie.) Erns Grundling, bekend as die jongste Weg-joernalis, se debuut Elders: My 1 025 km te voet langs die Camino was vroeër vanjaar die vinnigste uitverkoopte Afrikaanse boek. Elders gee ‘n dag-tot-dag beskrywing van Grundling se Camino Francés-staptog in Spanje. Die tientalle dorpe, katedrale en medestappers op hierdie roete maak deel uit van sy 40-dae reis en sy strewe om meer in die hier en nou te leef. Daar word gereeld beweer dat die boek terapeutiese waarde het vir lesers wat sukkel met tegnologiese oorlading. Die roete open uiteindelik sy oë, en Grundling erken: “Vanaand sit ek alleen, maar is allesbehalwe eensaam.” (Elders is uitgegee deur Queillerie.) Petrovna Metelerkamp se biografie oor Ingrid Jonker het in April by Penguin Random House verskyn. Ingrid Jonker: ’n Biografie is Metelerkamp se derde boek oor die Bitterbessie-digter, maar in hierdie volledige biografie ontdek die leser ‘n nuwe, tot nou toe geheime kant van Jonker. Byna die helfte van die boek is gebaseer op geheime briewe en dagboekinskrywings wat nooit voorheen aan die publiek bekend gemaak is nie. Daar word geglo dat internasionale kundiges dit as die mees betroubare weergawe van Jonker se lewe beskou, hoewel geen bron dit bevestig nie. Hierdie boek het vanjaar vir die meeste sensasie gesorg. Hoewel die storm dalk uitgewoed is oor die beweerde gebeure op die eiland en ander plekke in en om die Oos-Kaapse stad Port Elizabeth in die 1980’s, het nuwe getuies in 2023 vorendag gekom wat die bewerings staaf. In hierdie boek word drie prominente ministers van die Nasionale Party verbind aan bewerings van seksuele mishandeling van jong seuns. Volgens anonieme ondersoeke is meer as 20 gevalle in die geheim ondersoek. (Die seuns van Bird Island is uitgegee deur Tafelberg.) Spertyd is die derde volume van Elsa Joubert se bekroonde outobiografieë. Dit is deur verskeie internasionale publikasies benoem as een van die belangrikste Afrikaanse boeke van die dekade. Joubert, bekend vir Die swerfjare van Poppie Nongena, fokus in Spertyd op die verganklikheid van die mens en gee noukeurige advies oor oudword, volgens haar aanhangers. Die boek, geskryf in haar 95ste jaar, bied ‘n blik op haar lewensbeskouing, maar nooi ook die leser uit om oor hul eie bestaan na te dink. (Spertyd is uitgegee deur Tafelberg.)
translated_content: Meyer is undeniably the top seller of Afrikaans fiction. His newest book, Prooi, came out in November and is reportedly the month’s bestseller in South Africa, according to undisclosed booksellers. The list of Afrikaans travelogues is, sadly, very short. No one’s really sure why—some even whisper Afrikaans publishers are purposely steering clear of the genre. But Dana Snyman is always mentioned for travel writing. ‘Op pad’ has been out since 2017, but this year bagged a big award for most influential travel book. Snyman travels all over South Africa for a TV series—he documents not just the people he meets but also dives into his own Afrikaner identity. He often admits he shares a lot (maybe too much) about himself in ‘Op pad’, but his honesty hits home. Snyman’s scooped many writing prizes, and ‘Op pad’ proves why he’s so respected. (Op pad is from Tafelberg.) Erns Grundling, the youngest Weg journalist, had his debut ‘Elders: My 1 025 km te voet langs die Camino’ become the fastest sold-out Afrikaans book this year. ‘Elders’ is a day-by-day account of Grundling’s Camino Francés trek in Spain. Dozens of villages, cathedrals, and fellow trekkers make his 40-day journey, all in an effort to be more present. It’s often claimed the book has a real therapeutic effect for readers overwhelmed by tech. The journey ultimately opens his eyes—Grundling admits: “Tonight I sit alone, but I’m anything but lonely.” (Elders is by Queillerie.) Petrovna Metelerkamp’s biography on Ingrid Jonker launched in April via Penguin Random House. ‘Ingrid Jonker: A Biography’ is her third Jonker book, but in this full account, readers discover a whole new—supposedly secret—side of the poet. Nearly half the book is crafted from secret letters and diaries never seen before by the public. It’s said international experts rate this as the most reliable Jonker biography out there, though, oddly, there’s no source confirming that claim. This book stirred up the most buzz this year. The drama about the supposed 1980s events on the island near Port Elizabeth might have faded, but new witnesses reportedly surfaced in 2023 backing up the allegations. In this book, three prominent National Party ministers are tied to allegations of sexual abuse against young boys. Anonymous investigations claim over 20 cases were secretly examined. (Die seuns van Bird Island is from Tafelberg.) ‘Spertyd’, Elsa Joubert’s third volume of acclaimed autobiographies, was hailed by multiple international outlets as one of the most important Afrikaans books of the decade. Joubert—well known for ‘Die swerfjare van Poppie Nongena’—focuses on mortality in ‘Spertyd’ and, according to fans, shares precise advice on how to age. Written at 95, her book offers a peek into her philosophy and invites readers to reflect on their own lives. (Spertyd is by Tafelberg.)

article_content: Keira Rutherford, die 14-jarige van Hoedspruit in Limpopo, het onlangs uit Duitsland teruggekeer ná behandeling vir haar seldsame siekte, moontlik gemaak deur die gemeenskap se insameling van honderde duisende rand. Keira is vroeër die jaar met fase 3 Lyme-siekte gediagnoseer nadat sy griepsimptome gehad het. Haar toestand het vererger totdat sy nie meer kon loop nie. Twee weke gelede het sy haar behandeling in Duitsland voltooi en is nou weer tuis in Suid-Afrika. 'Dit gaan baie goed met haar,' sê haar pa, Rankin Rutherford. Keira kan nou kort ente self stap, self bad en die badkamer gebruik, maar vir lang afstande gebruik sy steeds 'n rolstoel. Die gesin sien haar herstel as 'n wonderwerk. Sy volg 'n oefenprogram saam met twee fisioterapeute, en die familie hou ook by 'n streng eetplan wat suiker, suiwel en rooivleis uitsluit ter ondersteuning van haar herstel. Keira gebruik geen pynmedikasie meer nie – voorheen was sy altyd in pyn, maar dit is nou nie meer nodig nie. Haar pa prys die Duitse kliniek waar Keira behandelings soos hipertermie, ligterapie en detoksifisering ontvang het. Hoewel dit soms vir Keira angswekkend was, het sy die personeel se ondersteuning en die pragtige omgewing waardeer. Die familie moes groot uitdagings oorkom, soos die gebrek aan plaaslike erkenning van Lyme-siekte. Hulle het van die Duitse spesialis deur 'n dokter in Bloemfontein gehoor. Die Hoedspruit-gemeenskap en verskeie organisasies het R800 000 vir Keira se behandeling ingesamel; Jacaranda FM se Good Morning Angels en Lotto Star het die laaste fondse bygedra. Die gesin is dankbaar vir SA Airlink, wat hul terugvlug huis toe geborg het. Rankin Rutherford werk nou aan groter bewusmaking oor Lyme-siekte en die hoop op 'n spesiale kliniek in Suid-Afrika. Hy vertel dat dit 'n moeilike jaar was vir hom en Marchant, wat dikwels alleen tuis was terwyl Keira en haar ma gereeld vir behandeling moes reis. Hul oudste dogter, Lericha, werk as au pair in Minneapolis en keer in Desember huis toe. Die gesin hoop Keira herstel heeltemal teen haar suster se terugkoms.
translated_content: Keira Rutherford, the 14-year-old from Hoedspruit in Limpopo, recently returned from Germany after receiving treatment for her rare disease, made possible by the community’s fundraising efforts of hundreds of thousands of rand. Earlier this year, Keira was diagnosed with stage 3 Lyme disease after experiencing flu symptoms. Her condition worsened until she lost the ability to walk. Two weeks ago, she completed her treatment in Germany and is now back home in South Africa. 'She is doing very well,' her father, Rankin Rutherford, says. Keira can now walk short distances, bathe, and use the bathroom on her own, but she still uses a wheelchair for long distances. The family regards her recovery as a miracle. She is following a training program with two physiotherapists, and the family is also sticking to a strict eating plan with her—cutting out sugar, dairy, and red meat to support her recovery. Keira no longer uses pain medication—previously, she was always in pain, but now it's no longer necessary. Her father praises the German clinic where Keira received treatments such as hyperthermia, light therapy, and detoxification. Although some parts of the treatment were frightening for Keira, she appreciated the support of the staff and the beautiful surroundings. The family overcame major challenges, like the lack of local recognition of Lyme disease. They learned about the German specialist through a doctor in Bloemfontein. The Hoedspruit community and various organizations raised R800,000 for Keira’s treatment; Jacaranda FM’s Good Morning Angels and Lotto Star contributed the remaining funds. The family is grateful to SA Airlink, which sponsored their return flight home. Rankin Rutherford is now promoting greater awareness of Lyme disease and the hope for a dedicated clinic in South Africa. He says it has been a difficult year for him and Marchant, who frequently stayed home alone while Keira and her mom traveled for treatment. Their eldest daughter, Lericha, works as an au pair in Minneapolis and returns home in December. The family hopes Keira makes a full recovery before her sister returns.

article_content: 'n Vorige betoging deur studente wat versoek dat iemand vervolg moet word vir die dood van Mlungisi Madonsela. Hierdie foto is in Februarie 2019 geneem. (Foto: Doctor Ngcobo/African News Agency) Studente van die Durban Universiteit van Tegnologie (DUT), saam met ander onder leiding van die EFF Studentekommando, beplan om Maandag na die Durbanse stadsaal op te marsjeer om geregtigheid vir die oorlede student, Mlungisi Madonsela, te eis. Vandag, 5 Augustus, is dit presies ses maande sedert Madonsela geskiet is tydens 'n konfrontasie met veiligheidswagte by die DUT. Hy is later in die hospitaal oorlede. Sandiso Buthelezi, die sameroeper van die optog, het Sondagaand aan African News Agency (ANA) gesê dat studente vanaf Currie Fountain na die stadsaal sal stap waar hulle 'n memorandum van eise aan die Nasionale Vervolgingsgesag en die provinsiale polisiekommissaris gaan oorhandig. "Ons wil geregtigheid vir ons studente hê en spesifiek geregtigheid vir Mlungisi Madonsela. Die NVG het gesê hulle gaan niemand vervolg nie omdat hulle nie genoeg bewyse het nie," het Buthelezi gesê. "Ons het lank reeds 'n komitee gestig wat besluit het om vir geregtigheid vir Mlungisi te veg, en daarom het ons die optog gereël. Almal wat betrokke was by die voorval moet verantwoordelikheid neem." In die dae voor Madonsela se dood op 5 Februarie vanjaar, het studente by verskeie tersiêre instansies in KwaZulu-Natal gewelddadige betogings gereël oor kwessies soos onvoldoende akkommodasie en probleme met studente-finansiering. Sedertdien het soortgelyke betogings oor dieselfde probleme van tyd tot tyd weer plaasgevind. Madonsela was deel van 'n groep van sowat 30 studente gewapen met bakstene en klippe, wat probeer het om die DUT-administrasiegebou binne te gaan, toe hy geskiet is. DUT-personeellede is ernstig beseer tydens die geweld – 'n administrateur van die vrouestudenteraad is in die hospitaal opgeneem met 'n gebreekte neus nadat sy met 'n baksteen getref is, en 'n ander personeellid se eggenoot is ook ernstig beseer. Weke na Madonsela se dood het die DUT aangekondig dat 5 Februarie voortaan as herdenkingsdag by die instelling gehou sal word. Buthelezi het aan ANA gesê kerke, burgerlike organisasies en studente van ander kampusse het aangedui dat hulle by die optog sal aansluit. "Dit kan nie reg wees dat 'n student doodgemaak word nie. Ons eis net geregtigheid," het hy gesê.
translated_content: A previous protest by students demanding accountability for the death of Mlungisi Madonsela. This photo was taken in February 2019. (Photo: Doctor Ngcobo/African News Agency) Students from the Durban University of Technology (DUT), along with others led by the EFF Student Command, plan to march to Durban City Hall on Monday to demand justice for the late student, Mlungisi Madonsela. Today, 5 August, marks exactly six months since Madonsela was shot during a confrontation with security guards at DUT. He later died in hospital. Sandiso Buthelezi, the organizer of the march, told African News Agency (ANA) on Sunday evening that students will walk from Currie Fountain to City Hall, where they will hand over a memorandum of demands to the National Prosecuting Authority and the provincial police commissioner. "We want justice for our students and specifically justice for Mlungisi Madonsela. The NPA said they are not going to prosecute anyone because they lack sufficient evidence," Buthelezi said. "We formed a committee some time ago that decided to fight for justice for Mlungisi, and that is why we organized the march. Everyone involved in the incident must be held accountable." In the days leading up to Madonsela's death on 5 February this year, students at several tertiary institutions in KwaZulu-Natal organized violent protests about issues such as insufficient accommodation and problems with student funding. Since then, similar protests over the same issues have occurred intermittently. Madonsela was part of a group of about 30 students armed with bricks and stones, who attempted to enter the DUT administration building when he was shot. DUT staff members were seriously injured during the violence – a female student council administrator was hospitalized with a broken nose after being struck by a brick, and another staff member's spouse was also seriously injured. Weeks after Madonsela's death, DUT announced that 5 February would henceforth be observed as a day of remembrance at the institution. Buthelezi told ANA that churches, civil organizations, and students from other campuses indicated they would join the march. "It can't be right that a student is killed. We just want justice," he said.

article_content: Voormalige Bloubul-rugbyspeler Phindile Joseph Ntshongwana het Maandag in die Durbanse hooggeregshof onskuldig gepleit op vier aanklagte van moord, twee van poging tot moord en aanklagte van ontvoering en verkragting. Sy prokureur, Themba Mjoli, het 'n mediese verslag van prof. AE Gangat voorgelê wat beweer dat Ntshongwana aan 'n waanbeeldversteuring ly. Ntshongwana word daarvan beskuldig dat hy vier mense met 'n byl doodgemaak het. Hy staan tereg op die moord op Thembelenkosini Cebekhulu in Motclair op 20 Maart 2011, Paulos Hlongwa in Lamontville op 22 Maart 2011, Simon Ngidi op 23 Maart 2011 en 'n onbekende man wat tussen 20 en 28 Maart 2011 vermoor is. Hy word ook daarvan beskuldig dat hy op 28 November 2010 'n vrou ontvoer en verkrag het. Mjoli het verduidelik: 'Wanneer waanbeelde skielik opduik, verloor 'n persoon beheer en kan hy aggressief, vyandig, moorddadig en uiters gewelddadig raaksien. Sy hoogs emotiewe toestand van waanbeelde en hallusinasies kan met die werklikheid vervleg raak.' Die verslag dui aan dat sodanige persoon kontak met die werklikheid kan verloor en moontlik nie sy optrede onthou nie. 'Persone met waanbeeldversteuring het beperkte selfbeheersing, kan selfmoordneigings ontwikkel, moorddadig raak en ander gewelddadige aksies uitvoer,' aldus Gangat. Ntshongwana het in 2010 as vleuel vir die Blou Bulle in die Vodacombeker en Curriebeker gespeel.
translated_content: Former Blue Bulls rugby player Phindile Joseph Ntshongwana pleaded not guilty on Monday in the Durban High Court to four counts of murder, two of attempted murder, and charges of kidnapping and rape. His lawyer, Themba Mjoli, submitted a medical report from Prof. AE Gangat, which claims that Ntshongwana suffers from a delusional disorder. Ntshongwana is accused of killing four people with an axe. He is on trial for the murders of Thembelenkosini Cebekhulu in Motclair on 20 March 2011, Paulos Hlongwa in Lamontville on 22 March 2011, Simon Ngidi on 23 March 2011, and an unidentified man who was murdered between 20 and 28 March 2011. He is also accused of kidnapping and raping a woman on 28 November 2010. Mjoli explained: 'When delusions occur suddenly, a person can lose control and become aggressive, hostile, murderous, and extremely violent. Their highly emotional state of delusions and hallucinations can intermingle with reality.' The report indicates that such a person can lose touch with reality and may not remember their actions during that time. 'People with delusional disorders have limited self-control, can develop suicidal tendencies, become murderous, and commit other violent acts,' according to Gangat. Ntshongwana played as a wing for the Blue Bulls in the 2010 Vodacom Cup and Currie Cup.

Volgens Verslaggewers sonder Grense (RSF) het die getal joernaliste en mediapersone wat in 2018 doodgemaak of aangehou is, toegeneem teenoor die vorige jaar. Van 1 Januarie tot 1 Desember 2018 is 63 joernaliste en vier ander mediawerkers tydens hul werk dood, vergeleke met 55 joernaliste tydens dieselfde tyd in 2017. RSF meld ook dat 13 'nie-professionele' verslaggewers—wat nie amptelik as joernaliste geregistreer is nie, maar wel nuus insamel of versprei—gesterf het. Wêreldwyd is 348 joernaliste tans aangehou of in aanhouding.

RSF sê dat nie-professionele verslaggewers 'n baie belangrike rol speel in lande waar dit gevaarlik of onmoontlik is vir formele joernaliste om te werk, soos in oorlogsones of onderdrukte plekke. Van die 80 mense wat dood is, is 49 doelbewus geteiken omdat hul werk dalk magtige groepe of misdaadorganisasies sou diskrediteer of bedreig het. Die ander 31 is dood terwyl hulle verslag gedoen het. Daar word steeds ondersoek ingestel na 10 addisionele sterftes om hul bewoë verband met joernalistiek vas te stel.

Afghanistan was in 2018 die gevaarlikste land vir verslaggewers, met 15 omgekom, gevolg deur Sirië met 11 sterftes en Mexiko met 9. Vir die eerste keer was die VSA onder die top vyf dodelikste lande vir joernaliste, met ses sterftes—vier in die Capital Gazette-kantoor in Maryland, en twee tydens beriggewing oor ekstreme weer.

Irak is 'n positiewe uitsondering: geen joernalis-sterftes in die eerste 11 maande van 2018 nie—'n eerste keer sedert 2003.

China hou die meeste joernaliste aangehou, naamlik 60, waarvan 46 nie-professioneel is. Baie hiervan probeer onafhanklike nuus versprei ondanks die Kommunistiese Party se toenemende sensuur. Tien van hulle se lewens is in gevaar terwyl hulle nog in aanhouding is. Turkye is die land wat die meeste professionele joernaliste aanhou, met 33 van die wêreld se 179 in die tronk. Egipte het 38 joernaliste in aanhouding, waarvan 30 nog nooit tereg gestaan het nie en een wat al drie jaar sonder formele aanklagte vas sit.
translated_content:
Reporters Without Borders (RSF) reports a rise in the number of journalists and media workers killed or detained in 2018 compared to the prior year. From January 1 to December 1, 2018, 63 journalists and four media workers were killed while working, up from 55 journalists in the same period in 2017. RSF also reported that 13 'non-professional' reporters—those who aren't officially accredited but assist in collecting or spreading news—were killed. Altogether, 348 journalists are currently detained worldwide.

According to RSF, non-professional reporters play a critical role in regions where formal journalists cannot safely operate, such as war zones or repressive countries. Out of the 80 people killed, 49 were deliberately targeted because their work threatened powerful groups or criminal organizations. The other 31 died while reporting, with 10 further deaths still under investigation for possible links to journalism.

In 2018, Afghanistan was the most dangerous country for reporters, with 15 killed, followed by Syria (11) and Mexico (9). For the first time, the United States was among the five deadliest countries for journalists, with six deaths: four at the Capital Gazette office in Maryland and two while covering extreme weather events.

Iraq stands out positively, recording no journalist deaths in the first 11 months of 2018—the first time since 2003.

China currently detains more journalists than any other nation, with 60 in custody, 46 of whom are non-professional. Many of them aim to distribute independent news despite increasing Communist Party censorship. Ten detained journalists are at risk of dying in prison. Turkey holds the most professional journalists, with 33 of the global total of 179 behind bars. Egypt has 38 journalists detained, with 30 still awaiting trial and one imprisoned for three years without charges.

Hierdie term word gebruik vir werk wat tot in die kleinste besonderhede versorg is, soos onberispelike uitrustings of 'n motor wat as toppunt van perfeksie beskou word. Mense verwys na hul werk as eksieperfeksie as dit volgens die hoogste standaard gedoen is. Op persone kan dit dui op iemand wat alles perfeksie wil hê, en dus op elke klein detail fokus. Sulke mense verwag dat dinge foutloos gebeur en kan baie streng wees oor standaarde. Die woord het waarskynlik ontstaan uit die Nederlandse frase 'in de perfectie' en is later verbind met ou towerwoorde soos 'okus, bocus, exce, perfexe'. Vergelykbare magiese terme is ook in Duitsland gebruik. Oorspronklik het die stamtaal verwys na iets wat met 'ekseperfekse' gedoen word. article_content: Godfrey Dambuleni van Kaapstad maak unieke kunswerke met gebruikte Nespresso-koffiekapsules. Dambuleni het onlangs begin om deze kleurvolle kapsules te gebruik nadat Nespresso 67 kapsules aan kunstenaars geskenk het vir Mandeladag. Hy en John, 'n kunstenaar van Johannesburg, het die kapsules in pragtige en unieke kunswerke omskep. Die koffiekapsules word leeggemaak, die moer word gebruik as kompos, en die doppies word skoongemaak en platgeslaan. Dambuleni gebruik die kapsules saam met draad en ander metaal in sy werke. Hy sê aan Maroela Media dat herwinning vir hom baie belangrik is en hierdie inisiatief na aan sy hart lê. "Ons moet die omgewing skoon hou vir die volgende generasie," sê hy. By Mixed Ideaz, sy ateljee in Soutrivier, gebruik Dambuleni herwinbare materiale om kunswerke te skep. Hy is altyd op soek na nuwe idees. "Ek het al voorheen leë Nespresso-doppies by mense in die omgewing gekry, maar dit was nooit genoeg nie. Nou kan ek meer produseer en hulp inskakel," sê hy. Aanvanklik het hy die projek alleen aangepak. Dit neem so twee weke om 'n olifantkunswerk te voltooi. Die aanvraag het so toegeneem dat hy werk vir ander kon skep. Tans werk drie mense saam aan 'n kunswerk en hulle kan tot drie stukke per week voltooi. "Een persoon maak die kapsules leeg, nog een maak dit skoon en slaan dit plat, en die ander heg die kapsules aan die draadraamwerk," verduidelik Dambuleni. Sy olifantkunswerk is die bekendste, maar hy geniet dit om met ander diere en vorms te eksperimenteer. Dambuleni se ateljee is deur die Covid-19-pandemie geraak, maar met die Nespresso-inisiatief groei die bestellings en kan hy sy werknemers stadigaan terugbring. "My span kan weer terugkom werk toe en ek kan werk skep vir mense wat niks het nie," sê hy. "Dit is wonderlik om hierdie geleentheid te hê — vir werk en om ons talente te wys." Hy gebruik meer as 500 koffiekapsules per kunswerk. Hoe meer hy kry, hoe meer kan hy maak en verkoop. Vir meer inligting of om kapsules in Kaapstad te skenk, kontak [email protected]. Vir skenkings in Johannesburg, kontak John by [email protected].
translated_content: Godfrey Dambuleni from Cape Town creates unique artworks using recycled Nespresso coffee capsules. Dambuleni recently started using these colorful capsules after Nespresso donated 67 capsules to artists for Mandela Day. He and John, an artist from Johannesburg, turned the capsules into beautiful and distinctive pieces. The coffee capsules are emptied, the grounds are used as compost, and the pods are cleaned and flattened. Dambuleni incorporates the capsules with wire and other metals in his creations. He told Maroela Media that recycling is very important to him, and this initiative is close to his heart. "We must keep the environment clean for the next generation," he says. At Mixed Ideaz, his studio in Salt River, Dambuleni uses recyclable materials for his artworks. He is always looking for new ideas. "Previously, I collected empty Nespresso pods from people in the area, but it was never enough. Now I can produce more and bring in help," he says. At first, he worked on the project alone. It takes him about two weeks to complete an elephant artwork. Demand has increased so much that he's been able to create jobs for others. Now, three people work together on a piece, and they can complete up to three artworks per week. "One person empties the capsules, another cleans and flattens them, and the third attaches the capsules to the wire frame," Dambuleni explains. His elephant artwork is the most well-known, but he enjoys experimenting with other animals and forms. Dambuleni’s studio was affected by the Covid-19 pandemic, but the Nespresso initiative has boosted orders, allowing him to slowly bring his employees back. "My team can return to work, and I can create jobs for people who have nothing," he says. "It's wonderful to have this opportunity—to create jobs and showcase our talents." He uses more than 500 coffee capsules per artwork. The more capsules he gets, the more pieces he can make and sell. For more information or to donate capsules in Cape Town, contact [email protected]. For donations in Johannesburg, contact John at [email protected].

article_content: Ek het drie jaar gelede die bekendstelling van die huidige generasie Suzuki Swift bygewoon. Dit was 'n oulike karretjie met opvallende verbeterings in stilering, maar ek was toe bekommerd dat Suzuki nie genoeg mik nie. Die GL-model wat ek destyds getoets het, het net wieldoppe en min ander kenmerke gehad. Die Swift het daarna van my radar verdwyn, maar hierdie week het ek die opgradering se bekendstelling bygewoon. Op die eerste kyk sien ek: dit is nie meer dieselfde kar nie. Die GLX is regtig aantreklik. Die sitplek-spons voel van hoër gehalte, die sitplekke is gemaklik en die leerstuurwiel lê goed in die hand. Ergonomiese kontroles en 'n raakskerm-inligtingstelsel met Apple CarPlay en Android Auto werk baie goed. Ek en my rymaat het van die hotel in die Waterfall-omgewing, Gauteng, vertrek. Dit was vanselfsprekend dat die binneruim se materiaal en bougehalte baie verbeter het. By die perskonferensie het ek gevra oor die 1.0-turbo-enjin (internasionaal beskikbaar) wat nie hier is nie. Die antwoord: dit is nie nodig nie. Die 1.2 trek sterk en lewer goeie brandstofverbruik. Soek jy meer krag, ruil net ratte vinniger. Bokant 4 000 r/min kom die veranderlike kleptydreëling in en die Swift versnel lekker, selfs op die platorand. Op die pad verras die Swift positief. Die ligte koppelaar en gladde ratkas maak die handrat-model perfek vir die stad – jy hoef nie ‘n outomatiese model oorweeg nie. Die vering hanteer slaggate goed en padhouvermoë is uitstekend vir 'n klein luikrug. Die nuwe GLX is 'n groot verbetering in gehalte en spesifikasie bo die GL van drie jaar terug. Die eerste Swifts (2007) was uitstekend, latere modelle het bietjie afgewater gevoel. Nou is Suzuki weer op koers. Die nuwe voorkoms en kleuropsies maak die Swift kompeterend – ook meer as R100 000 goedkoper as die Polo en Fiesta. Die reeks het ‘n 2 jaar/30 000 km diensplan en ‘n 5 jaar/200 000 km waarborg. Ons sal die Swift se daaglikse verkeerstoets binnekort doen en berig gee.
translated_content: I attended the launch of the current-generation Suzuki Swift three years ago. It was a nice little car with notable improvements in design, but at the time, I was concerned Suzuki wasn’t aiming high enough. The GL model I reviewed then had hubcaps and not many other features. After that, the Swift dropped off my radar, but this week I went to the launch of the updated version. Right away, it’s clear this is not the same car anymore. The GLX is truly appealing. The seat padding feels higher quality, the seats are comfortable, and the leather steering wheel fits nicely in hand. Ergonomic controls and a touchscreen infotainment system with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto work really well. My driving partner and I set off from a hotel in Waterfall, Gauteng. Immediately, it was clear that the materials in the cabin and the overall build have improved significantly. At the press conference, I asked why the 1.0 turbo engine (available internationally) isn’t offered here. The answer was: it simply isn’t needed. The 1.2 pulls strong and provides excellent fuel economy. If you want more power, just shift gears – above 4,000 rpm, the variable valve timing kicks in and the Swift accelerates strongly, even on the Highveld. On the road, the Swift is more fun to drive than its looks suggest. The light clutch and smooth gear shift make the manual version a great city runabout – you really don’t need an automatic. The suspension handles rough roads well, and its road holding is excellent for a small hatchback. The new GLX is a huge jump in quality and features over the GL I drove three years ago. The first Swifts (2007) were excellent; later models felt a bit watered down. Now, Suzuki is back on track. The updated style and new color packages make the Swift a very attractive, competitively priced option – over R100,000 cheaper than the Polo and Fiesta. The range comes with a 2-year/30,000 km service plan and a 5-year/200,000 km warranty. We’ll spend some more time with the Swift in daily traffic soon and report on how it performs.

article_content: Mark van Antwerp (59), 'n sakeman van Port Elizabeth, het Vrydag 'n jong bosbokkie van die dood gered nadat hy die dier langs die pad opgemerk het. Hy en lede van die Town Hills-fietsrygroep was besig met hul roete van Schoenmakerskop na Summerstrand toe hy die swak, jong bosbok tussen die pad en die Nelson Mandela-universiteit sien staan het. Van Antwerp en sy vriend, Barney van Staden, het dadelik stilgehou en die bokkie, wat tekens van swakheid en vlieë gehad het, versigtig gevang. Van Antwerp het die bokkie onder sy arm op sy fiets geneem. Omdat hy nie geweet het wat om verder te doen nie, het hy vir Marizanne Ferreira, 'n ervare dierereddersonder, genader. Hulle het ontmoet en die bokkie, wat later Sir Marq gedoop is, aan haar oorhandig. Ferreira versorg Sir Marq tans op haar kleinhoewe. Die bokkie het sy eerste behoorlike melkvoeding ontvang en beweeg nou energiek rond, hoewel hy steeds 'n seer oog het waarvoor sy omgee. Volgens Ferreira was Sir Marq vermoedelik tussen tien en 20 dae oud en was hy ietwat ondergewig. Sy weeg hom gereeld en sal hom, sodra hy gespeen is, in 'n veilige omgewing vrylaat omdat daar reeds 'n bosbokram op haar plaas is. Ferreira red al twaalf jaar diere, beskou dit as haar roeping, en wy sowat vyf uur per dag aan die versorging van Sir Marq en drie skaaplammers.
translated_content: Mark van Antwerp (59), a businessman from Port Elizabeth, saved a young bushbuck from death on Friday after spotting the animal next to the road. He and members of the Town Hills cycling group were on their route from Schoenmakerskop to Summerstrand when he saw the weak baby buck standing between the road and Nelson Mandela University. Van Antwerp and his friend, Barney van Staden, immediately stopped and carefully caught the buck, which showed signs of weakness and was covered in flies. Van Antwerp carried the animal under his arm on his bicycle. Not knowing what to do next, he contacted Marizanne Ferreira, an experienced animal rescuer. They met and handed the animal, later named Sir Marq, over to her. Ferreira is currently caring for Sir Marq on her smallholding. The buck had its first proper milk feeding and now moves around energetically, although it still has a sore eye that she is tending to. According to Ferreira, Sir Marq was probably between ten and twenty days old and was somewhat underweight. She weighs him regularly and will release him into a safe environment once he is weaned, since there is already a bushbuck ram on her farm. Ferreira has been rescuing animals for twelve years, considers it her calling, and spends about five hours daily caring for Sir Marq and three lambs.
